evidence.description: The owner-approved exception records. The approved waivers depend on its exact text.
Every known difference between bdhx and upstream bd v1.2.1, grouped by topic, with its tracking task.

Runs each scenario with bdhx and the pinned upstream oracle in fresh disposable workspaces and compares stdout, stderr, exit code and, for most cases, the files of the workspace. The required parity-smoke lane runs it on linux/amd64 with a CGO build on every pull request and main push.
Compares the Haxe export read with upstream bd export --all.
The acceptance tests a to i of the snapshot extension spec (BHX-M08-09).
The legacy-config tests and the configfile.Load( guard of the workspace facade.

differences.summary: With BD_DEBUG set, bdhx prints none of upstream's debug lines, except from code in a native facade.

source.quote: With `BD_DEBUG` set, upstream prints its debug lines on stderr, and `bdhx` does not.

differences.summary: A BEADS_DB or BD_DB path that selects another path makes where and store commands refuse.

source.quote: When `BEADS_DB` (or, for `where`, `BD_DB`) selects with another path

differences.summary: config get of a user-global key and config show refuse when the user config.yaml exists.

source.quote: `config get` of a user-global key (`metrics.*`, `node_id`) and `config show` report that they are not available yet

differences.summary: config validate and config drift refuse with --global and when a server or central config is set.

source.quote: `config validate` and `config drift` also report that they are not available yet with `--global`

differences.summary: Cycle detection starts at issues in byte order of their IDs, one of upstream's random results.

source.quote: `bdhx` starts the walk at the issues in the byte order of their IDs

differences.summary: A BEADS_DOLT_DATA_DIR or dolt_data_dir without .beads/embeddeddolt makes store commands refuse.

source.quote: a data directory that `BEADS_DOLT_DATA_DIR` or `dolt_data_dir` names makes upstream create the embedded database

differences.summary: A --db workspace whose metadata.json cannot be read or decoded makes store commands refuse.

source.quote: When `--db` selects a workspace whose `.beads/metadata.json` cannot be read or does not decode

differences.summary: For a redirect into a detached commit worktree, bdhx waits for Git without upstream's 5-second limit.

source.quote: upstream stops each Git command of its branch-worktree choice after 5 seconds

differences.summary: Some reads open the store fewer times than upstream, so they print Dolt's in-progress directory warning fewer times.

source.quote: skipping in-progress database directory

differences.summary: In a .beads/.env file that is not valid UTF-8, bdhx changes each invalid byte to U+FFFD.

source.quote: `bdhx` changes each invalid byte to U+FFFD

differences.summary: events tail --follow and events prune report that they are not available yet.

source.quote: `events tail --follow` and `events prune` report that they are not available yet.

differences.summary: Where upstream output order is random (Go map order), bdhx prints one fixed order.

source.quote: `bdhx` prints one fixed order.

differences.summary: bdhx does not create a missing workspace gate lock file, so it reads without that lock.

source.quote: `bdhx` does not create it, so it reads without that lock and prints the same output.

differences.summary: bdhx opens gate lock files read-only, so an unwritable lock file gives no ungated warning.

source.quote: `bdhx` takes the lock and prints no warning.

differences.summary: graph refuses when upstream would look up an external dependency in another repository.

source.quote: dependency in another repository.

differences.summary: label list-all reports not available yet in a proxied workspace.

source.quote: `label list-all` reports that it is not available yet in a proxied workspace.

differences.summary: A workspace with only a legacy config.json makes where and every store command refuse; with --db, version and help print the same output but write nothing.

source.quote: This is a recorded exception

differences.summary: A list --format template that needs upstream's Go types runs in a Go facade without the limit hint and partial output.

source.quote: `bdhx` runs these templates in a Go facade on upstream's types

differences.summary: At a gate stop, a list --format template that needs upstream's Go types stops instead of listing the database.

source.quote: So `bdhx` prints the same warning and then stops with `Error: list is not available yet on a database behind the binary in this build`

differences.summary: list --watch --ready reads the query of list --ready --json in every workspace.

source.quote: `list --watch --ready` reads the query of `list --ready --json` in every workspace.

differences.summary: On macOS, bdhx takes the stored letter case of a path from directory listings, not F_GETPATH.

source.quote: On macOS, `bdhx` takes the stored letter case of a path from the names that its directories list.

differences.summary: bdhx does not trust the macOS Shared folder for redirects, so it prints the redirect warning fewer times.

source.quote: Upstream also trusts the macOS Shared folder

differences.summary: Store commands refuse when the embedded store lacks the selected database, which upstream creates.

source.quote: when the embedded store has no database with the name that `.beads/metadata.json` selects

differences.summary: bdhx never writes upstream's automatic backup to .beads/backup.

source.quote: `bdhx` never writes a backup.

differences.summary: Ready reads do not wake expired defers first, so a woken issue is missing from the ready list.

source.quote: `bdhx` never writes, so such an issue stays deferred and is missing from its ready list

differences.summary: For an unknown command, bdhx prints no Did you mean list.

source.quote: For an unknown command, `bdhx` prints no `Did you mean this?` list.

differences.summary: bdhx does not check the workspace identity at the pre-run of commands outside upstream's readOnlyCommands.

source.quote: `bdhx` does not check the workspace identity yet.

differences.summary: Without metadata.json, store commands refuse when the embedded store has no beads database.

source.quote: In a workspace without `.beads/metadata.json`, every command that reads the database prints upstream's warning

differences.summary: bdhx never migrates a database whose schema is behind the binary; it stops with upstream's --readonly error.

source.quote: `bdhx` never migrates. It stops with upstream's `--readonly` error and leaves the database unchanged.

differences.summary: bdhx prints no tips and records no tip time in the database.

source.quote: `bdhx` prints no tips.

differences.summary: Workspace lookups do not include upstream's Git worktree and jj workspace fallbacks.

source.quote: these lookups do not include upstream's Git worktree and jj workspace fallbacks

differences.summary: Without a stored issue_prefix, partial issue IDs resolve with the config.yaml prefix instead of upstream's guess.

source.quote: `bdhx` uses the prefix from `config.yaml` instead.

differences.summary: bdhx refuses ready --claim.

source.quote: `bdhx` refuses `ready --claim`

differences.summary: In a server-mode or proxied workspace, ready --explain derives blocked issues and cycles without the stored flag and full dependency tables.

source.quote: `ready --explain` cannot read the stored `is_blocked` flag or the full dependency tables yet

differences.summary: Where the remote-migrate gate lets upstream migrate or fast-forward, bdhx stops with a not-available error.

source.quote: Where the gate lets upstream write, `bdhx` stops

differences.summary: Commands refuse where upstream would read an issue or planning store of another repository through routing.

source.quote: the routed reads themselves wait for routing and shared stores

differences.summary: In a server-mode workspace, contributor auto-routing takes its settings only from config.yaml and the environment.

source.quote: contributor auto-routing takes its settings only from `config.yaml` and the environment

differences.summary: These commands read embedded workspaces only and report not available yet in a server-mode or proxied workspace.

source.quote: read embedded workspaces only. In a server-mode or proxied workspace they report that they are not available yet.

differences.summary: In a server-mode or proxied workspace, the human ready view uses the ready --json query for wisps.

source.quote: `bdhx` reads the human `ready` view through the native facade, with the query of `ready --json`.

differences.summary: The schema version check of a server-mode or proxied workspace is not compared and probably prints a different error.

source.quote: so they do not compare the schema version check of a server-mode or proxied workspace

differences.summary: Every store command reports not available yet in shared-server mode and when the db setting names a database.

source.quote: Every command that reads the database reports that it is not available yet in shared-server mode

differences.summary: show reads .beads/last-touched but never writes it.

source.quote: `bdhx` reads that file, for `show` without an ID, but never writes it

differences.summary: bdhx adds the hidden snapshot command, which upstream reports as an unknown command.

source.section: `bdhx snapshot` is a hidden BeadsHX extension
source.quote: Upstream bd v1.2.1 has no such command

differences.summary: In a server-mode or proxied workspace, stale --json records have no labels field.

source.quote: the records of `stale --json` have no `labels` field

differences.summary: A usage error that upstream finds later prints no redirect warning first.

source.quote: it prints no redirect warning before the error

differences.summary: The write subcommands of ported groups report that they are not available yet, and dep asks for a read subcommand; writes come with M09.

source.quote: The write subcommands of ported groups fail too

waivers.upstreamBehavior: In a workspace whose .beads directory has a valid legacy config.json and no metadata.json, upstream bd v1.2.1 rewrites config.json as metadata.json and runs the command. With a --db path it also rewrites the file for version and bd help <command>.
waivers.beadshxBehavior: where and every command that reads the database exit 1 with: Error: <command> is not available yet when the workspace has only a legacy config.json in this build (or the same message as a JSON error document with --json). version, help pages and unknown commands match upstream; with a --db path they print the same output and write nothing.
waivers.userImpact: Store commands refuse in a legacy-only workspace until upstream bd migrates the file once.
waivers.migrationImpact: None. bdhx leaves config.json in place.
waivers.reason: The migration is a persistent write, and the M08 read-only profile makes none. Migration belongs to M12.
waivers.requesterDisposition: Approved by the repository owner (fullofcaffeine) on 2026-11-22, including the refusal wording and the removal milestone (beadshx-m08-03.3).
waivers.reviewTrigger: When M12 (schema, migration, backup, doctor and recovery parity) starts.
waivers.removalCondition: Remove the refusal when M12 ports the legacy config migration, and turn the legacy-config refusal cases into exact comparisons with upstream.
waivers.rollback: Run the pinned upstream bd once in the workspace with a command that opens the store, such as bd where. It migrates the file, and bdhx then reads the workspace normally.
waivers.upstreamFallback: Use the pinned upstream bd for the first command in a legacy-only workspace.

waivers.upstreamBehavior: bd snapshot prints: Error: unknown command "snapshot" for "bd".
waivers.beadshxBehavior: bdhx snapshot prints a read-only task snapshot artifact (schema beadshx-task-snapshot/1, JSON Lines) of an embedded workspace on stdout. The command is hidden, so the root help stays byte-equal to upstream; it refuses server-mode, shared-server, proxied and --global workspaces.
waivers.userImpact: A new, hidden, read-only command. The artifact holds the task text, so it must not go to a public repository.
waivers.migrationImpact: None. The artifact is derived; delete it at any time and run the command again.
waivers.reason: BHX-M08-09 asks for an optional deterministic task snapshot with the native revision, for parity, Caf and recovery consumers. Upstream has no command that gives the issue records together with the revision they come from.
waivers.requesterDisposition: Approved by the repository owner (fullofcaffeine) on 2026-11-22, as spec v1 of BHX-M08-09, including the name, the hidden command and the all-issues record set.
waivers.reviewTrigger: When upstream adds a snapshot command, when the Caf consumers (M10-11, M19-03, M19-05) start to read the artifact, and before any change to the header keys, the record set, the record encoding or the order.
waivers.removalCondition: Rename the command if upstream takes the name. A change to the header keys, the record set, the record encoding or the order needs a new _schema number.
waivers.rollback: Stop using the command; nothing reads the artifact yet.
waivers.upstreamFallback: Upstream bd export --all prints the same issue lines, in another order and with memory lines; bd-upstream import restores a workspace from the artifact.

source.section: `bdhx snapshot` is a hidden BeadsHX extension
